correctness.rationale: The construction gives an ideal \(D=k^{(\Omega)}\) and an injective polynomial part with \(R/D\cong k[x,y,z]\). A prime containing \(D\) is therefore a unique pullback from the polynomial ring. A prime not containing \(D\) omits exactly one coordinate idempotent; the complementary idempotent then forces the prime to equal that coordinate evaluation kernel. This exhausts all primes. Infinite fibers plus Zariski density force every idempotent polynomial part to be \(0\) or \(1\), giving exactly finite/cofinite coordinate idempotents. All consequences on minimality, clopens, irreducible components, and dimension are direct from that exhaustive classification.
